npcs.name: Brunhild Keelwright
npcs.greet: I rivet hulls for the Stormcloak fleet. My great-grandfather built ships that sailed the other way.

npcs.name: Skjold Whale-Eye
npcs.greet: Forty years on the Sea of Ghosts. I've seen things on the ice I don't tell my wife about.

npcs.name: Magistra Ulrika Varo
npcs.greet: If you've come about the overdue library books, I returned them. Mostly.

npcs.name: Maveri Sadras
npcs.greet: You have the look of someone who goes places. Unwise places. Excellent.

npcs.name: Rashida at-Taneth
npcs.greet: You carry your blade like you've used it. Good. Talk to me.

npcs.name: Jaffir the Lamp-Seller
npcs.greet: Lamps, oil, wicks. Light for every dark place. Except the one I need.

npcs.name: Lieutenant Calaenor
npcs.greet: You may address me as Lieutenant. You may not touch the charts.

npcs.name: Gwaelin Saltbelly
npcs.greet: Fish? No fish. The sea is eating our boats, and the Green Pact says nothing about eating the sea back.

npcs.name: Brother Cassian Velle
npcs.greet: Stendarr's mercy on you. Have you come to light a candle for the crew of the Blessed Gull? Everyone does.

npcs.name: Keeps-the-Tally
npcs.greet: Every debt is a root. Pull one, and you find the whole tree.

relics.name: Ulfvar's Ice-Log
relics.desc: A logbook frozen into a block of clear ice, the last page legible through it.

relics.name: The Cold Hearthstone
relics.desc: A round stone that burns with blue flame and gives off no heat at all.

relics.name: Heart of the Moot-Cairn
relics.desc: A lump of ancient ice that never melts, with something dark at its centre.

relics.name: Dragonguard Oath-Scroll
relics.desc: A silk scroll in Akaviri script, signed in old brown blood by nine names.

relics.name: Skin of the Ice-Drum
relics.desc: A drumhead of pale hide, rimed with frost, that still trembles when the wind blows.

relics.name: Hazadir's Unblooded Sword
relics.desc: A Ra Gada blade of fine old steel without a single nick along its edge.

relics.name: Nhalar's Dig Diary
relics.desc: A field diary; the last pages list the diggers' names, each crossed out in order.

relics.name: Maormer Mist-Lantern
relics.desc: A lantern of blue glass whose light seems to push fog aside.

relics.name: Stolen Serpent Egg
relics.desc: A leathery egg the size of a man's head, warm, packed in Woodhearth sawdust.

relics.name: Sload Covenant
relics.desc: A contract written on dried kelp. The last signature belongs to a priest of Stendarr.

relics.name: The Coral Ledger
relics.desc: Pages of pressed coral, each etched with names and the debts owed by their great-grandchildren.

side_atm_landfall: Nothing moves on the Atmoran shore. The pines are cased in ice to their tips, and the wind makes them ring like glass.
A longship stands upright a short way inland, frozen into a wave of ice that never broke.
side_atm_longhouse: Draugr sit at the long tables of the drowned longhouse, cups raised to a hearth that burns blue and gives no warmth.
One of them wears a Skyrim sailor's cloak, faded red, with a keel-and-hammer brooch at the throat.
Don't take the stone. We lit it, and it lit us. Eighty years at this table. Take it home and your whole hall will sit down with us.
side_atm_moot: The giants come out of the snow one by one and lay a block of ice on the cairn. Each block steams with cold.
When the cairn is high enough, the sea freezes to the south. Then we walk to the warm land, and the little men's halls become our larders.
side_aka_bone_beach: The beach is made of bones. Ribs as tall as ships' masts lean against each other, polished by the tide.
Dragon skulls line the path inland, each one carved with coiling serpent script, as if to say: these were ours to eat.
side_aka_shrine: You come for the Dragonguard's oath. They left it here as a promise: hunt every dragon in the west, and send the last of them home to us.
They never sent it. The oath is broken. Their blood is ours to collect.
side_aka_drum: In a hall of blue ice an old Kamal sits alone, beating a great drum with a bone, slow and steady.
Sleep, sleep. The host sleeps while the drum speaks. Haskarr wants silence. Silence wakes the host. Let the drum speak, small warm one.
side_yok_tomb: The tomb lies half under the sea. Salt water laps at the feet of stone Ra Gada warriors lining the hall, swords raised.
A child of my line sends a champion. Good. Come, then, and see what I was.
side_yok_hazadir_truth: This sword never tasted blood. When the Doom came, I put my family on the first ship and I did not look back.
Tell her. Tell my descendant what her ancestor was: a coward who lived, so that she could.
side_yok_dig_camp: The dig camp is abandoned. Tents flap over empty bedrolls, and a long, smooth trench winds away into the dunes.
Every tent has been rolled flat in the same direction, as if something huge passed through looking for one thing.
side_yok_nhalar_reveals: Jaffir sent you? Dear Jaffir. He thinks I came for scrolls. I came for the Ra Gada sleeping under this sand, and the Mother wanted payment for the way.
I paid her. One digger a night. Now they dig for me.
side_pya_mist_parts: The mist hangs like a wall over the water, then parts in a tunnel exactly where your boat sails, closing again behind you.
On the shore, a lantern of blue glass burns on a coral post. Someone wanted you to find the way.
side_pya_thessaril_speaks: Your Lieutenant's grandfather burned our coast with the fleet of Alinor. My grandmother sang the first mist that night, so they could never find us again.
Carry the lantern back to him, and his ships will come through the wall. Or break it. Either way, I will not let you leave with it.
side_pya_rookery: Nests of woven kelp line the cove, each the width of a cart. Most are empty and torn apart. Woodhearth sawdust is scattered on the sand.
So the tree-folk send a champion. Your harbor stole our eggs, warm-blood. The Old Coil only wants her children back.
side_thr_congregation: Drowned sailors stand knee-deep in the surf, facing out to sea, singing a hymn of Stendarr in voices full of water.
Each one wears the patch of the Blessed Gull on his shoulder.
side_thr_chapel: A full crew, delivered as promised. One soul kept back, as agreed, to tell the tale on the shore. Your priest signs a careful hand.
side_thr_vault: Every debt is written. Every debt is due. I have waited four thousand years for these names to ripen. I can wait while you die.

quests.title: The Cold Hearth
quests.pitch: Ulfvar Keelbreaker. He took a longship to Atmora eighty years ago, to fetch the hearthstone of our clan's first longhouse and light it again in Windhelm. He never came back. I've built the ship he'd have wanted. I'm too old to sail it. You aren't.
quests.desc: Brunhild Keelwright of Windhelm asked me to sail to Atmora and learn what became of her great-grandfather Ulfvar, who went to fetch his clan's ancient hearthstone.

objectives.text: Make landfall on the frozen coast of Atmora
Drive off the wraiths around Ulfvar's frozen longship
Chip Ulfvar's log out of the ice
objectives.journal: Ulfvar's last entry: 'Found the longhouse. Lit the stone. It burns blue. So cold. The others sit down at the tables and will not rise.'

objectives.text: Find the drowned longhouse in the frozen forest
Break the hearth-guard of the first Atmorans
Kill Ysgrim Hearth-Jarl
objectives.journal: Ysgrim Hearth-Jarl fell beside his blue fire. Ulfvar did not rise to fight me. He only lowered his cup.

objectives.text: Take the cold hearthstone from the fire-pit
Tell Brunhild what you found in Atmora
objectives.topic: I found Ulfvar. He's been sitting at that stone's fire for eighty years.
objectives.reply: And you brought the stone. Of course you did; that's what I asked. Now tell me what to do with it.

choices.label: Drop it in the deepest water in the harbor.
choices.reply: Aye. Let it burn blue at the bottom of the sea, where no fool can sit down by it. Ulfvar would want that.

choices.label: Keep it, but never light a hall with it.
choices.reply: A warning on the mantel, then. The clan will tell the story every Midwinter. Ulfvar earned that much.

quests.outro: Ulfvar Keelbreaker still sits at his table in Atmora, but the fire that held him has gone out. Brunhild carved his name on her new ship's prow.

quests.title: The Hoar-King's Moot
quests.offer: What did you see on the ice?
quests.pitch: Frost giants. A dozen of them, on the Atmoran shore, piling ice blocks into a cairn as tall as the Jarl's longhouse. Every week it's taller, and every week the pack ice comes a little further south. The whales are fleeing. I think the sea is fleeing. Go and look, and if it's what I think, knock it down.
quests.desc: Skjold Whale-Eye of Dawnstar saw frost giants building a great cairn of ice on the Atmoran coast, and the pack ice has been creeping south ever since.

objectives.text: Land on the Atmoran shore where Skjold saw the giants
Fight past the giants guarding the approach
Hide near the Moot-Cairn and watch the giants gather
objectives.journal: The giants meant to freeze the Sea of Ghosts solid and walk across it into Skyrim. Their Hoar-King was laying the last blocks himself.

objectives.text: Kill Ymrvald the Hoar-King
Dig the heart out of the Moot-Cairn
objectives.journal: Inside the cairn lay an Atmoran war-axe frozen in clear ice, its edge still white with frost. It had been feeding the cairn's cold for longer than the giants could remember.

objectives.text: Bring Skjold the heart of the cairn
objectives.topic: The cairn is broken. This was inside it.
objectives.reply: The pack ice went out of the bay this morning, all at once, like a door opening. Keep the axe. A thing like that belongs in a hand that knows what it cost.

quests.outro: The Moot-Cairn of Atmora is a heap of slush now, and the whales are back off Dawnstar. I carry the axe that froze a sea.

quests.title: The Broken Oath
quests.pitch: The Dragonguard. The Akaviri who came west with their swords and stayed to guard the emperors. Every history says they swore an oath before they sailed, and left it in a shrine on the serpent coast of Akavir. Nobody has ever read it. I am too old for boats. You, I suspect, are not too wise for them.
quests.desc: Magistra Ulrika Varo of Solitude asked me to find the Dragonguard's founding oath, left long ago in a Tsaesci shrine on the coast of Akavir.

objectives.text: Land on the serpent coast of Akavir
Cross the field of dragon bones
Find the tidal shrine beyond the bone field
Kill Vhezhar the Coil-Priest
Take the oath-scroll from the shrine's altar
objectives.journal: The oath was not to guard emperors. Nine Akaviri swore to hunt the dragons of Tamriel and send the last one alive to the serpent-kings. The Blades' great tradition began as a hunting contract.

objectives.text: Bring the oath to Magistra Ulrika
objectives.topic: The Dragonguard's oath. You'll want to sit down.
objectives.reply: A hunting contract. Signed in blood. Every heroic ballad about the Dragonguard just turned into a bill of sale. What on Nirn do I do with this?

choices.label: Publish it. History should be true, even when it stings.
choices.reply: Then the Imperial Library will have a very uncomfortable autumn. Good.

choices.label: Seal it away. Some debts are better forgotten.
choices.reply: Sealed, then. In the vault, under my own key. I'll sleep worse for it, I think.

quests.outro: The Dragonguard's oath has left Akavir after two thousand years. Vhezhar's katana, carried by the last Coil-Priest, came with me.

quests.title: The Ice-Drum of Kamal
quests.pitch: Drums. In Kamal, the frozen north of Akavir. Our grandmothers still tell how the snow demons came over the ice to Morrowind. My scrying-bowl has frosted over every night this month, and I hear a drum beating under the frost. Find that drum and destroy it, before it calls them south again.
quests.desc: Maveri Sadras of Sadrith Mora hears a war-drum in her scrying-bowl and fears the Kamal will march again. She asked me to destroy it.

objectives.text: Land on the frozen shore of Kamal
Fight through the Kamal outriders
Follow the drumbeat to the hall of blue ice
objectives.journal: The drum wasn't calling the Kamal to war. It was keeping them asleep. The war-chief Dir-Haskarr wanted it silenced.

objectives.text: Kill Dir-Haskarr before he silences the drum
Return to Maveri in Sadrith Mora
objectives.topic: I found your drum. Destroying it would have woken the whole host.
objectives.reply: A lullaby. I heard a lullaby and called it a war-song. Well. I suppose I owe the north an apology. What did you do with it?

choices.label: I left the old drummer beating it.
choices.reply: Then let him play. I'll listen every night, and if he ever stops, I'll know to run.

choices.label: I cut a scrap of the drumhead as proof.
choices.reply: A frozen skin that trembles on its own. Delightful. I'll study it very, very carefully.

quests.outro: The Ice-Drum of Kamal still beats, slow and steady. Dir-Haskarr will not be waking anyone.

quests.title: The Unblooded Sword
quests.pitch: My family descends from Hazadir the Unbroken, a captain of the Ra Gada. His tomb lies on one of the drowned isles of old Yokuda, and his sword with him. My grandfather tried to reach it and came back with one hand. I want that sword. I'll pay for a champion who can stand where he couldn't.
quests.desc: Rashida at-Taneth of Sentinel wants the sword of her ancestor Hazadir the Unbroken, a Ra Gada captain buried on a sunken isle of Yokuda.

objectives.text: Land on the sunken isles of Yokuda
Find Hazadir's half-drowned tomb
Defeat the tomb's Ra Gada guardians
Duel Hazadir the Unbroken
Take Hazadir's sword from his bier
objectives.journal: Hazadir's blade had never drawn blood. He fled the Doom of Yokuda on the first ship. The family's legend was built on a man who chose to live.

objectives.text: Bring the sword to Rashida
objectives.topic: Your ancestor's sword. And his last words.
objectives.reply: Not a nick on it. Speak. What did he say?

choices.label: He ran from the Doom so his children could live. You exist because he wasn't brave.
choices.reply: ...Then I'll carry an honest blade. My grandfather's hand, and his lie, can rest. Thank you for the truth.

choices.label: He fought to the last. The sword is clean because he never missed.
choices.reply: Ha! Never missed. I'll have that carved on the hilt.

quests.outro: Hazadir's sword hangs in Rashida's house in Sentinel, still unblooded. The ghost on the sunken isle is quiet.

quests.title: Mother of Dunes
quests.pitch: My partner Nhalar hired thirty diggers and sailed to Yokuda to find a library buried in the dunes. Half a year now. No letters, no ship. He bought every lamp I had on credit. I want the money, but more than that, I want to know he's alive.
quests.desc: Jaffir the Lamp-Seller of Stros M'Kai asked me to find his partner Nhalar, who led thirty diggers into the Yokudan desert and never came back.

objectives.text: Land on the desert coast of Yokuda
Find Nhalar's dig camp in the dunes
Kill the scorpions nesting in the camp
Kill Kesheth, Mother of Dunes
Take Nhalar's diary from the serpent's trench
objectives.journal: Nhalar's diary listed his diggers by name. One name was crossed out every night, beside the words 'payment to the Mother'.

objectives.text: Follow the diary to the buried tomb
Kill Nhalar the Sand-Priest
Bring Jaffir the diary
objectives.topic: I found Nhalar. Read this before you ask me anything.
objectives.reply: Thirty names. I sold him the lamps they died by. Keep the debt; I'll not take a coin of his. I'll send what's left to the diggers' families, every septim.

quests.outro: The Mother of Dunes is dead, and so is the man who fed her. Jaffir sold his shop to pay thirty families.

quests.title: Through the Mist
quests.pitch: The Maormer hide their isles behind a wall of mist that no Altmer navigator has pierced in an age. Our agents report the Tide-Singers keep a lantern that parts it. Bring it to me, and the Sea Vipers will never again strike our coast from hiding. You will be paid as befits a minor instrument of Alinor's will.
quests.desc: Lieutenant Calaenor of Alinor wants the Maormer mist-lantern, which lets ships pass through the fog that hides Pyandonea.

objectives.text: Sail through the mist wall to Pyandonea
Fight the Maormer raiders on the beach
Take the mist-lantern from its coral post
Defeat Thessaril Tide-Singer
Return to Lieutenant Calaenor in Alinor
objectives.topic: I have the lantern. The Tide-Singer told me why the mist exists.
objectives.reply: Ancient history, embellished by pirates. The lantern, please.

choices.label: Here. Do what you will with it.
choices.reply: Adequate work. The fleet sails within the season. You may go.

choices.label: I broke it on the way back. The mist stays.
choices.reply: You... broke it. How regrettable. Take your fee and leave my sight before I find a law you've broken.

quests.outro: I have seen the hidden coast of Pyandonea, and whether anyone else will depends on what I did with a blue glass lantern.

quests.title: The Serpent's Herald
quests.offer: The sea is eating your boats?
quests.pitch: A serpent the length of the harbor wall, with a Maormer riding on its neck like a stable-boy on a pony. Seven boats this season. Our hunters say kill the rider and the beast goes home. Our hunters are very hungry. So are we. Sail south and kill the rider.
quests.desc: Gwaelin Saltbelly of Woodhearth says a sea serpent ridden by a Maormer herald has sunk seven fishing boats this season.

objectives.text: Sail south to the herald's coast on Pyandonea
Survive Vorrhaal the Old Coil
Find the serpent rookery in the cove
objectives.journal: Woodhearth sawdust in the empty nests. Someone in my own harbor has been stealing serpent eggs, and the herald came to take them back.

objectives.text: Fight the herald's guard
Kill Iriel Wave-Rider
Take the egg Iriel recovered from Woodhearth
Bring the egg back to Gwaelin
objectives.topic: This egg came from Woodhearth's harbor. Your people stole them first.
objectives.reply: The harbor master's crates. He swore they were Elsweyr melons. By the Pact, we'd have eaten a serpent egg if we'd known. Hungry or not, a stolen egg is a stolen child.

choices.label: Hang the harbor master's name in the market and send the egg home.
choices.reply: Both. Today. Let the sea see we can be honest too.

choices.label: Raise it. Woodhearth could use a guardian of its own.
choices.reply: A serpent of our own... The elders will howl. I like it.

quests.outro: The boats of Woodhearth fish again, and nobody in the harbor will touch a crate of 'melons'.

quests.title: The Drowned Congregation
quests.offer: What happened to the Blessed Gull?
quests.pitch: Her whole crew walked over the rail one calm night off the coral isles and into the sea, singing. I alone was left alive on a lifeboat. Now sailors say they hear the hymn from the water near Thras. I must know they're at rest. Will you go where I can't bear to?
quests.desc: Brother Cassian Velle of Anvil was the only survivor of the Blessed Gull, whose crew walked into the sea off Thras. He asked me to lay them to rest.

objectives.text: Land on the coral shore of Thras
Release the drowned crew of the Blessed Gull
Find where the hymn is coming from
Break through the dreugh guarding the coral chapel
Kill the Sload Thallomuth
Take the kelp covenant from the Sload's lectern
objectives.journal: The covenant traded the crew of the Blessed Gull for safe passage, one soul kept back as witness. It was signed by Brother Cassian Velle.

objectives.text: Confront Brother Cassian with the covenant
objectives.topic: Your signature is on this, Brother.
objectives.reply: The ship was sinking. The Sload offered to calm the sea. I thought it meant only the sea. I have lit a candle for every one of them, every night, for two years.

choices.label: Candles aren't enough. Tell Anvil the truth.
choices.reply: Yes. From the pulpit, this Sundas. Stendarr is the god of mercy, not of hiding.

choices.label: They're at rest now. Carry it yourself.
choices.reply: I will carry it. Every day. Thank you for setting them free.

quests.outro: The hymn no longer rises from the water off Thras. In Anvil, Brother Cassian still lights his candles.

quests.title: The Coral Ledger
quests.pitch: Our egg-mothers say the Sload never forget a debt. They write them in coral and wait for them to ripen. Now Lilmoth's hatchlings dream of a slug reading their names aloud. The water has a long memory. Go to Thras, find the book, and make it forget.
quests.desc: Keeps-the-Tally of Lilmoth believes a Sload keeps a coral ledger of debts owed by Argonian clans since the old plague wars, and that it means to collect.

objectives.text: Land on the reefs of Thras
Fight off the reef dreugh
Kill Old Shell-Mother
Find the coral vault beneath the reef
Destroy the vault's drowned clerks
Kill Ghaavorth the Patient
Take the Coral Ledger
objectives.journal: Ghaavorth's ledger held four thousand years of debts, page after page of Argonian clan names, with Keeps-the-Tally's own near the end.

objectives.text: Bring the ledger to Keeps-the-Tally
objectives.topic: Here is every debt the Sload ever wrote down.
objectives.reply: So heavy. So many names. Even mine. What should become of it?

choices.label: Grind it to sand and give it back to the sea.
choices.reply: Sand forgets. The sea forgets. Then Lilmoth may forget too. Good.

choices.label: Read the names to the Hist, so the roots remember them freely.
choices.reply: Remembered by roots, not by slugs. Yes. The Hist will hold them gently.

quests.outro: Ghaavorth the Patient waited four thousand years and collected nothing. Lilmoth's hatchlings sleep without dreams of slugs.
